question: Should OpenClaw adopt this AI-safety taxonomy as a permanent core and plugin SDK contract, and if so which host-owned trust, lifecycle, and persistence model must it use?
rationale: The branch creates a new security-sensitive plugin capability and several public operator surfaces; code repair cannot safely choose whether the API exists, which events plugins may assert, or whether the dashboard promises durable audit history.

options.title: Redesign the full contract
options.body: Keep the feature direction but require host-derived provenance, an injected plugin emitter, lifecycle-owned exporter/store subscriptions, canonical persistence, and real end-to-end proof before merge.

options.title: Land a narrower core taxonomy
options.body: Limit the first change to internal host-emitted event contracts and exporter mappings, deferring plugin emission, Gateway APIs, CLI, and UI until the contract stabilizes.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Close or pause the PR until the linked feature issue receives explicit sponsorship for a core diagnostics and plugin API expansion.

recommendation.title: Redesign the full contract
recommendation.body: Keep the feature direction but require host-derived provenance, an injected plugin emitter, lifecycle-owned exporter/store subscriptions, canonical persistence, and real end-to-end proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history spans the plugin SDK, manifest/runtime ownership, browser seams, and gateway authorization affected by this decision.
